column1: # 30 fps, the Switch's own rate: in the first field the GPU takes about 58 ms a frame (16 fps) at 60, so 60 is out of reach there. game.tsv's fps_target 60
# stays for iOS; porter port --fps60 brings 60 back (its DM_FPS_TARGET=60 row comes after this one in env.txt)
env
# Measured at the Cobblestone Tor autosave (AYN Odin 2, Turnip R8, 30 fps target, 600-frame means from the log). Docked 1080p as ported: GPU busy 63 ms,
# vkQueueSubmit 50 ms, frame p50 66.7 ms (15 fps).
# With Turnip a submission that signals a timeline semaphore blocked in vkQueueSubmit for 50 ms a frame; with the fence ring it takes 0.13 ms (as PR #365 found
# on the same device). No picture change.
env
# Turnip's GMEM (tiled) rendering cost more than it saved for this game's many render passes: sysmem rendering took GPU busy 63 -> 53 ms docked, and the
# screenshot was identical. Other Vulkan drivers ignore the variable.
env
# Docked 1080p with both rows above still took 53 ms of GPU (frame p50 54 ms, 18 fps), so 30 fps was out of reach. Handheld mode is the game's own
# lower-resolution output, as on a Switch held in the hands: the same spot took 19 ms of GPU and held 30 fps, and the busiest view of the field took 36 ms
# (26-27 fps). With the game's own dynamic resolution working (game.tsv gpu_tick_rate) docked holds 30 fps too, at a lower resolution, but handheld stays the
# default: it draws less, so it runs cooler and drains the battery less. Docked is a pause-menu switch away.
# Battery at the same spot, 2 minutes each with both rows above and dynamic resolution: handheld 1.21 A (GPU busy 23 ms, frame p50 33.2 ms), docked 1.62 A
# (GPU busy 29 ms, frame p50 33.4 ms). Capping the GPU clock at 475 or 401 MHz drew the same 1.21-1.24 A in handheld, and GMEM rendering drew 1.20 A with
# GPU busy 27 ms, so neither is used.
